policy: Original core mechanics are authoritative; modern presentation must not change economic outcomes; modern gameplay additions must be opt-in.

mechanics.title: Per-player weekly turns
mechanics.target: One turn per player; week advances after all players finish.
mechanics.current: Turn order supports 1–2 humans and AI; 4-human original maximum unavailable. v0.5.36 applies Classic per-player reliability decay on turn close and journals ordered hotseat/AI/weekly phases; original four-player maximum remains unavailable. v0.5.37 adds source-identified startTrn state 4 computer bonus ($20–$100 cash at 1/7); other source states remain provisional. v0.5.38 records source state 10 food-loss and state 18 wardrobe warning outcomes in the bounded Classic weekly journal; execution timing and spoilage chances are still compatibility rules. v0.5.41 adds independent Classic relaxation decay (source state 6, floor 10) and recorded state-20 quarterly loan status; rest recovery and loan default penalties remain provisional.
mechanics.acceptance: Four humans complete a week in correct order without taking actions for each other.

mechanics.title: 60-hour weekly budget
mechanics.target: Start each player turn with 60 hours, original modifier exceptions recorded.
mechanics.current: Classic uses 60h (Modern retains 40h), hunger penalties still simplified. v0.5.36 checks clock/phase transitions against a deterministic saved journal, without changing provisional travel-time conversion. v0.5.56 forces original-inspired homeward return by default; route shortfall is deducted from the next week; selectable deviations are stored in the game snapshot. v0.5.59 allows in-venue zero-duration Classic trades at 0 remaining hours, without allowing new travel; house-rule ten-action cap defaults off.
mechanics.acceptance: Fresh game starts with 60 hours; no duplicated time deductions; imported games handled by migration policy.

mechanics.title: Movement and building entry
mechanics.target: Distance-based movement; entering a building costs 2h.
mechanics.current: v0.5.33 introduces original `steps + 2 * 20` tick estimate per nonempty ring leg, and charges +2 Classic clock units on entering Employment Office; the 170-step waypoint graph remains authoritative. Actual waypoint-to-60-unit clock conversion is a separate explicitly provisional adapter; all moves quote and spend atomically. v0.5.37 keeps all 13 Classic geographic venue cells stable on phone/desktop with pan/fit; geometry and road projection are presentation-only, not new travel costs. v0.5.38 phone Overview tap selects/zooms without charging travel; only the Explore action triggers the usual host-authoritative travel and animated camera follow. v0.5.41 adds an optional presentation-only Skip Animation control, which never submits another movement action or charges the clock. v0.5.59 audits seven version-matched DOS route index legs with read-only SCI tick scenarios, but original player movement-duration conversion remains unverified and unchanged. v0.5.72 corrects the source AI tick model from provisional 20 to active global475=14 (room1.sc:1066,1315), and audits all 156 directed routes against carry-dependent bounds. These are NOT verified player movement charges; live travel remains unchanged until DOSBox evidence.
mechanics.acceptance: Move around ring, reenter building, track exact expected time with original observations.

mechanics.title: Action time accounting
mechanics.target: Full work session 6h paid for 8h; job application 4h; study 6h; relaxing 6h.
mechanics.current: v0.5.34 retains DOS work-entry reliability priority (< requirement−5 dismissal; otherwise warning if < requirement−2 on first attempt of week), pre-pay/time; full and partial work still grants one capped stat step per successful action. Source tick/clock conversion remains provisional. v0.5.35 adds saved reconciled Classic paychecks and net-aware AI forecasts, but the original temp0/temp1 debt branch remains unverified. v0.5.53: source-backed Employment late-week four-unit charge cap and separate DOS tick audit; route-to-player units still provisional. v0.5.59 removes the speculative 10-venue-action cap from Classic default, preserving it as optional weeklyActionLimit; zero-hour transactions now work at the current venue.
mechanics.acceptance: Full and partial work, success/failure application and study action charge documented hours.

mechanics.title: Single job, workplace locking
mechanics.target: Exactly one primary job; work only at its workplace; switching replaces role.
mechanics.current: Implemented with explicit switch confirmation. v0.5.34 adds once-per-week work warnings and pure gross/net paycheck quote. DOS special rent garnishment using full gross and temp overwrite is not yet byte exact. v0.5.35 adds saved reconciled Classic paychecks and net-aware AI forecasts, but the original temp0/temp1 debt branch remains unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Two hired positions never coexist; former employer denies shifts; current one allows work.

mechanics.title: Applications and openings
mechanics.target: Requirements + chance-based no openings; failed applications still consume time.
mechanics.current: Classic 37-job catalog with eligibility filter; agency now selects employer first and lists that workplace’s jobs, with optional future applications, 4h failed attempts, and chance-based no openings. Exact DOS UI ordering and RNG unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Under-qualified and no-opening attempts use original rejection/time rules.

mechanics.title: Work-stat gains and caps
mechanics.target: +1 experience/+1 dependability per work session up to job/degree caps.
mechanics.current: Classic XP/Dependability +1 per full six-hour work-credit up to job+degree caps; partial hours accumulate across actions and weeks, resetting upon changing job or dismissal. Original DOS partial-stat edge cases unverified. v0.5.34 adds once-per-week work warnings and pure gross/net paycheck quote. DOS special rent garnishment using full gross and temp overwrite is not yet byte exact. v0.5.35 adds saved reconciled Classic paychecks and net-aware AI forecasts, but the original temp0/temp1 debt branch remains unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Repeated entry-job shifts reach cap, not infinity; changing jobs/degrees affects cap.

mechanics.title: Dependability and firing
mechanics.target: 20 initial, -3 per week; low stat warnings and dismissal on work attempts.
mechanics.current: Classic starts Dependability 20 and decays 3/week; hiring below 10 resets it, low reliability warns, and work attempts below job requirement−5 dismiss without pay. Exact messages/DOS edges unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Week decay, hire minimum, warning threshold and firing reproduced with seeded results.

mechanics.title: DOS-floppy employment catalog
mechanics.target: 37 original DOS positions with employer, base wage, XP, Dependability, diplomas and uniforms; preserve CD-only distinction.
mechanics.current: 37 documented floppy positions implemented in Classic data; two CD-only jobs omitted; shared modern building venues not 1:1; exact DOS binary comparison pending.
mechanics.acceptance: Every Classic role is tested against the documented table, with no Modern Story catalog changes.

mechanics.title: Wages and raises
mechanics.target: 8h pay for full 6h work, current wage; raise prerequisites, wage changes and risks.
mechanics.current: Classic: 8-hour wages for 6h worked; fractional wages are carried between partial shifts without repeated floor rounding. Remainder resets when changing/dismissing job; raises, original economic variability and exact DOS partial-pay rules still need observation. v0.5.34 adds once-per-week work warnings and pure gross/net paycheck quote. DOS special rent garnishment using full gross and temp overwrite is not yet byte exact. v0.5.35 adds saved reconciled Classic paychecks and net-aware AI forecasts, but the original temp0/temp1 debt branch remains unverified. v0.5.36 moves source-derived −3 weekly dependability to player endTurn, prior to next-week action reset.
mechanics.acceptance: Pay matches applied wage, raise refusal/cost, garnishment and role switching exact.

mechanics.title: Eleven branching degrees
mechanics.target: 11 permanent named degrees with prerequisite edges and possible multi-course progress.
mechanics.current: 11 named diplomas and original prerequisite graph now feed 37 DOS job qualifications; course availability/end-condition and original implementation variants still unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: All 11 degrees reachable through correct graph; job-specific combinations enforced.

mechanics.title: Course time and benefits
mechanics.target: Enroll fees and 6h lessons, usually 10 lessons; studies can benefit from durables.
mechanics.current: Classic enrollment $50, ten 6h lessons (1–5h partial final time permitted), computer and three-book study aids, graduation +5 happiness/reliability. Enrollment queue and item details require DOS validation.
mechanics.acceptance: Enroll, alternate courses, complete 10 lessons, adjust for valid aids, graduate.

mechanics.title: Weekly uniform consumption
mechanics.target: Three tiers, weekly wear including unworn; higher tier satisfies lower; budget/premium durations.
mechanics.current: Implemented week-based casual/formal/business clothing with tier substitution.
mechanics.acceptance: An unused outfit ages each week; expired uniform blocks work; superior outfit substitutes.

mechanics.title: Durables and supply market
mechanics.target: Durables have benefits, wear/breakage/theft risks; shops rotate stock.
mechanics.current: Classic tracks specialty versus discount appliance condition, failures, Socket City repairs, loss of benefits and low-cost-housing theft. Exact rates unverified; Modern unchanged.
mechanics.acceptance: Buying durable modifies right mechanic; breakdown, theft and changing stock reproducible.

mechanics.title: Rent cycle and debt
mechanics.target: Rent due every 4th week; manual payment/extensions; garnishment/arrears consequences.
mechanics.current: Classic cash-paid rent on 4-week cycle; $325 base in low-cost housing; Pass-2 DOS d12 extension approval thresholds (0=100%, 1=75%, 2=50%, 3+=25%) and once-per-week guard. Garnishment and due-state ordering still provisional. v0.5.61: original n108.sc garnishment comparator is read-only; live arrears/fees remain provisional, because DOS partial work can pay above earned gross. Four-week rent cycle retained and not falsely certified.
mechanics.acceptance: Choose rent office payment; miss it and observe prescribed arrears, garnishment, extension.

mechanics.title: Weekly food and storage
mechanics.target: Fresh food/fast food choices, perishability, fridge and weekend consequences.
mechanics.current: Classic food 1/2/4 bundles use original goods price integer formula and current bounded seeded consumer index. Exact full EconomicIndex trend drift not yet recovered; fixed $1 newspaper/$10 lottery bundle unaffected. Food capacity and spoilage remain partial. v0.5.57 adds a closing-week identity to food event audits and moves meal accounting into a pure reducer, without changing the original-unknown spoilage probability. v0.5.60: no-food state 14 cash stress now source-labeled; merged original consumable identities still incomplete. v0.5.61: source state 10 -2 happiness on unrefrigerated discarded fresh food and -1 on refrigerated over-cap losses; original storage-before-consumption order is documented, but active meal-before-storage compatibility remains until source consumables and AI migrate.
mechanics.acceptance: Compare 4-week food inventory with/without fridge; validate spoiled food and week events.

mechanics.title: Bank, loans and investments
mechanics.target: Savings; loans/repayment; investment categories; differing liquid-cash risk.
mechanics.current: Classic separate six-stock broker with documented base prices, $100 deposits/withdrawals, no savings interest, loans and $45 principal+$5 interest payments, defaults. Volatility/credit approval formula and random crash/theft remain approximate/missing. v0.5.61: state 20 loan due is checked on completed weeks 4/8/12, no new fees; first missing monthly payment creates a notice rather than invented -3 happiness. Later-month -1 uses approximate paySched projection; exact credit/paysched remains incomplete.
mechanics.acceptance: Document and replicate loan interest/default, 6 markets, cash theft exposure.

mechanics.title: Pawn, repossession and durable economy
mechanics.target: Pawn valuables, redeem within time window, other players can buy unredeemed goods.
mechanics.current: Dedicated Pawn Shop in Classic, provisional pawn/redeem, recovered property, shared lot state and resales; exact prices and deadlines unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Pawn item, redeem within window, let it expire, other player buys it.

mechanics.title: Economic cycles and random losses
mechanics.target: Events may cause robberies, job loss, weekends; timing differs by DOS edition.
mechanics.current: Classic lottery now uses one original 0..500 roll per ticket stack with $5,000/$500/$200 thresholds; tickets always cleared. Goods index and lottery outcomes journaled. Other weekly events/robbery/theft probabilities and full SCI ordering remain partial. v0.5.60: DOS state 12 no-food happiness −2, state 14 no-food cash-stress with exact branch/roll bounds; state 24 source happiness mapping tested pure but not tied to synthetic economic phase. Complete DOS event RNG/item parity still missing. v0.5.61: spoiled fresh food state 14 d2 source comparator (local6=-1) added pure; active event execution remains no-food only until item identities migrate.
mechanics.acceptance: Edition-specific seeded economic/robbery weekend events follow original windows and effects.

mechanics.title: Four adjustable goals
mechanics.target: Wealth, happiness, education and career; win when all chosen thresholds achieved.
mechanics.current: Classic tracks individual goal points 10–100 and 200-point default. Human targets and Jones targets now differ: Take It Easy +40, Play Fair 0, Go For Broke -40. A seeded semi-random allocator distributes valid AI goals and keeps Wealth within 10 points of human wealth when feasible; exact Sierra allocation unverified. v0.5.57 introduces optional UX goal presets (30/50/75 points per objective) and Custom, without changing victory equations. v0.5.58 applies source-derived target-weighted progress with four independent raw-threshold victory gates. Original initial values and target difficulty distribution remain partially unverified.
mechanics.acceptance: Known reference states produce expected goal scores and victory trigger.

mechanics.title: Education/career scoring
mechanics.target: Money goal accounts for net worth including the value of owned goods (Sierra printed Quick Reference); education goal advances with completed university study units; Career follows dependability when employed.
mechanics.current: v0.5.58 uses source-derived integer Classic wealth points (including provisional durable appraisal), education 0 with no completed degrees else 1+9 per completed diploma, and employed career min(100,floor(Dependability/8)*10), zero unemployed. Printed Quick Reference mentions study units; exact partial-study contribution conflicts with reconstructed source and needs DOS runtime resolution. Asset appraisal/debts remain provisional.
mechanics.acceptance: Compare all four formula outputs against original observations, including unemployment.

mechanics.title: Optional modern content isolation
mechanics.target: Original rule outcomes must be same with cosmetic/UI modernizations.
mechanics.current: Classic original-style jobs, rent, bank and fresh-food services isolated from Modern Story, whose original 19 jobs, auto-rent, generic investments, savings interest and groceries are unchanged. World era remains cosmetic.
mechanics.acceptance: Classic ruleset suppresses non-original mechanical bonuses while keeping dialog optional.

notes_v0539: Presentation-only journey and original weekly source-state 12/34 journal. No claim that 34 payout/cooldown or original event order is accurately emulated.
notes_v0553: Classic Employment explicit 4-unit action charges cap at remaining 1–3 as in room1.sc timeKeep; source AI route ticks are NOT a calibrated player clock conversion. Modern unchanged.
